summary.headline: Midwest Ltd FY26 consolidated revenue rose 3% to INR645 crores; Q4 EBITDA margin 27.0% and PAT margin 16.5%, with Quartz start-up weighing on profitability.
summary.overview: Midwest reported FY26 consolidated revenue of INR645 crores, up about 3% from INR626 crores, with consolidated EBITDA margin of 27.01% (vs 27.43%) and PAT margin of 16.49% (vs 17.17%). Q4 revenue was INR215 crores, with EBITDA margin of 27% (vs 23.7% in Q3) and PAT margin of 17.16% (vs 13.48%). Granite standalone held margins at 27.55% EBITDA and 17.47% PAT, while the new Quartz segment absorbed about INR6 crores of cost in the year. Management said Quartz began full production in April 2026 and targets about 60% utilisation of its 300,000 tonne installed capacity in FY27, with Phase 2 commissioning expected in Q4 FY27. Debt fell by INR50 crores and working capital days fell from 122 to 104.

segments.name: Granite
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA margin 27.55% and PAT margin 17.47% in FY26, marginally up year on year. Management guides 10-12% organic growth; a Q4 logistics disruption from the war left about 3,000+ CBM unshipped, worth about INR25 crores of revenue.

segments.name: Quartz (processing)
segments.commentary: New segment; full production began in April 2026 after initial technical issues, with about 2,000 tonnes in the first month and targets of about 5,000 tonnes and 10,000 tonnes in the following months. Q4 sales were about 1,000+ tonnes, turnover about INR1.8 crores, and it drove about INR6 crores of cost in the consolidated numbers.

segments.name: Diamond wire
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR25 crores vs about INR16 crores in the comparative period, with PBT margin about 15%.

guidance_outlook: Granite organic revenue growth of 10-12% per year, with 10-13% cited for FY27 as the base case.
Quartz targets at least 60% utilisation of the 300,000 tonne Phase 1 capacity in FY27, with quarter-on-quarter growth; margins expected to improve beyond about 70% utilisation.
Phase 2 Quartz plant (300,000 tonnes, capex INR125-130 crores) to be commissioned in Q4 FY27, with revenue from Q1 FY28.
Price increase of about 4% negotiated with export buyers for the coming year to offset a 4-5% cost impact from fuel.

Long-term target (3-4 years): about INR1,000 crores from granite, INR400 crores from Quartz (two phases plus HPQ), INR350-400 crores from Sri Lanka HMS and about INR200 crores from the KMML project, implying about 2.5x top line.
capex_capacity: Quartz Phase 1: installed capacity 300,000 tonnes, with 80% (240,000-250,000 tonnes) treated as the practical peak; split about 70% engineered stone and 30% solar glass (solar priced about INR7,000/tonne; engineered stone INR9,000-14,500 ex-plant).

Quartz Phase 2: build started April 2026, capex INR125-130 crores, commissioning targeted Q4 FY27, with the first products engineered stone and solar, and HPQ following about a quarter after commissioning.
HPQ (high-purity quartz): about 20,000 tonne plant planned; the target is to be operational in about nine months.
Rare earths: a pilot plant with KMML (six months, about INR20 crores budget, mobile unit), starting around early July 2026, followed by a commercial plant in about 8 months and about a year to build.

Sri Lanka heavy mineral sands: exploration licence being converted to a mining licence after the government's new policy (expected June 2026); plant construction planned to begin around August, taking 9-12 months.
Captive solar: about 1 MW operating; a further 0.6 MW to be ordered; renewables about 10% of energy need, with the goal of replacing fossil fuel on trucks with EVs.
demand_pricing: Granite demand strong in domestic and Chinese markets; exports of blocks to Middle East, Algeria and Egypt added as new markets, with those buyers switching from slabs to blocks.
Quartz (solar) realisation about INR7,000/tonne ex-plant; engineered stone realisation INR9,000-14,500/tonne across four grades.
Off-take for HPQ expected to be mainly China (crucible makers) initially, with India about 2-3 years away; management says it has cut out about 5-6 months from the supply chain.
Energy costs about 17-18% of total cost, now about 12-13% fossil-based; fuel price increases are causing 4-5% cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the YoY PAT decline and sustainable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Granite standalone is intact (EBITDA 27.55%, PAT 17.47%). Quartz start-up costs and fixed costs of about INR6 crores reduced PAT to INR106 crores from INR112 crores, and margins should stabilise as utilisation rises.

qa_highlights.question: Diamond wire contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue about INR25 crores vs about INR16 crores earlier; PBT margin about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Quartz Phase 2 capex and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex INR125-130 crores; tendering equipment; commissioning by Q4 FY27 with revenue from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Quartz volume and margin outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Target at least 60% of 300,000 tonne capacity (about 150,000 tonnes); peak achievable 75-80%; margins to improve beyond about 70% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Sri Lanka HMS licence status?
qa_highlights.answer: Exploration licence paperwork submitted; conversion to mining licence to follow the new government policy, expected around June-July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: PLI for magnets and oxide strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Study in progress; by next quarter management expects clarity. Management sees oxides as the bigger gap (PLI demand about 2,500-3,000 tonnes vs IREL about 400 tonnes) and a magnet plant costs about INR1,000-1,300 crores.

risks_watch: Quartz ramp-up pace: the 60% utilisation target depends on stabilising the plant after earlier batch and quality issues (Q4 reprocessing and about 3,000-4,000 tonnes of production not sold).
Logistics and freight costs following the war (from end-February 2026) and ship availability; about INR25 crores of granite revenue slipped into the next quarter.
Fuel price inflation (4-5% cost impact) versus the about 4% price increase; FX assumptions.
Regulatory timing: Sri Lanka HMS policy and mining licence, KMML pilot start in July, and the government's Quartz auction framework.
Thorium and PLI strategy remain unclear; management says clarity may take about a year (Thorium) and about one quarter (PLI).
Related-party entity Midwest Gold (magnets, separate management) and the Sierra Leone subsidiary, with no concrete progress disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on granite and the Quartz ramp-up, but cautious on timelines: several projects (Sri Lanka HMS, HPQ, PLI) depend on government policy or equipment timing, and management gave few numeric answers on magnet and Sierra Leone plans.

So, Quartz we have started full production starting last month.
Now obviously where the demand is coming from, today if you ask me, majority of the off-take will still be China.

growth.why: Management guides Granite organic growth of 10-12% (FY27 base case 10-13%), backed by a ~4% export price increase, new block export markets and Quartz Phase 1 ramp to at least 60% utilisation of 300,000 t in FY27; Phase 2 (INR125-130 cr) is under construction for Q4 FY27 commissioning, but no firm order book numbers were given for the growth guidance.
